item.title: The stock market is anything but normal right now — and these charts show it
item.description: The S&P 500 is trading just shy of record territory, even as most individual stocks are struggling.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Adinolfi

item.title: I’m in my 20s and keep getting laid off. Should I invest in my employer’s 401(k) or look into other options?
item.description: “I have lost faith that the traditional career spanning decades at one company even exists anymore.”
item.dc:creator: Aditi Shrikant

item.title: TV dinner overload? The frozen-food aisle may be too crowded for its own good.
item.description: Industry giant Conagra Brands has so many frozen-food items that they’re competing against each other, an analyst says.
item.dc:creator: Bill Peters

item.title: Three reasons this Wall Street market-making powerhouse says investors should reload on stocks right now
item.description: September provided a stock-market reset, pointing to a good end to the year, says Scott Rubner of Citadel Securities.
item.dc:creator: Jamie Chisholm

item.title: Here’s the bond-market alternative as U.S. and other developed markets debt deteriorate
item.description: Jefferies’s Christopher Wood says bonds of the Group of Seven have been in a “structural bear market” since March 2020.
item.dc:creator: Nora Redmond

item.title: Brazil is holding an election — and for the stock market, there’s more to gain than to lose, says fund manager
item.description: Were Flavio Bolsonaro to outperform current polling Sunday, an emerging-market fund manager see the opportunity for a sharp rally in stocks
item.dc:creator: Jules Rimmer

item.title: My wife never went back to work after raising our kids. Do I have to share my retirement savings 50/50?
item.description: “For 14 years I have gotten up every morning and gone to work while she has been free to pursue whatever interested her.”
item.dc:creator: Quentin Fottrell

item.title: Another viral AI-doomsday report claims ‘it’s over.’ Why home prices could take a hit as screen-based jobs disappear.
item.description: Egan-Jones has become the latest to issue a viral AI-doomsday report, zeroing in on difficulties facing screen-based workers and the housing market.
item.dc:creator: Barbara Kollmeyer

item.title: ‘I don’t want to die on the sales floor’: I’m 67 and earn $19.50 an hour at a big-box store. When can I finally retire?
item.description: “I started taking Social Security at 66 and receive $2,410 a month. I have $214,000 in my 401(k).”
item.dc:creator: Quentin Fottrell

item.title: Amazon is hiking chip-rental prices and reportedly moving Nvidia processors off the balance sheet
item.description: In a sign of the financing crunch facing the hyperscalers financing the AI revolution, Amazon has announced it is raising prices on how much it charges to rent high-performance microchips as it reportedly is going to sell and then lease back Nvidia chips.
item.dc:creator: Steve Goldstein
